factorRatings.note: The Infatuation calls the oval pies inventive but close to classic, with crisp edges and a chewy (if sometimes soft-bottomed) crust, singling out the fennel sausage pie and truffle-cheese mushroom pie; a MyNorthwest roundup of Tom Douglas's 'pizzeria with a bread-baker's soul' rates the dough among the best in the city thanks to olive oil and sea salt on the crust edges.

The Infatuation rates this New York-style slice shop 8.5/10, praising a 'stunning crispy crust' and balanced sauce-to-cheese ratio, calling the curled, crunchy pepperoni cups and the cheese slice 'an instant classic,' and flagging the Sicilian pepperoni square as a must-try despite the unassuming storefront.

Coverage frames this as a bar first and pizzeria second: The Infatuation highlights face-sized slices and Sunday karaoke as reasons to visit with a big group, while a Seattle Weekly review of the 28-inch pies and $4.95 slices praised the heavily topped, sausage-and-pepperoncini 'Sinatra' slice and noted the sauce runs sweet.

The Infatuation scores this Neapolitan mini-chain location 7.3/10, praising a charred crust that holds up best with simple toppings -- the Margherita DOC with buffalo mozzarella and San Marzano tomatoes is called the best pie -- while knocking the pistachio-puree Roberto pie for tasting too much like peanut butter.

The Infatuation scores this Capitol Hill Neapolitan spot 7.6/10, calling it a 'perfect middle-tier' option rather than the neighborhood's top pizza pick -- reliable, romantic and easy to walk into on short notice, recommending the margherita with buffalo mozzarella or the spicy salami pie.

The Infatuation rates this Phinney Ridge Chicago deep-dish spot 8.6/10 and says it's worth crossing town for, praising the puffy, deep crust with a near-burnt caramelized-cheese edge and naming the sausage-pepperoni-bacon 'Meatza' a standout; KOMO's Seattle Refined profiles owner Dave Lichterman's house-made dough and generous toppings, including his own favorite, the pineapple-and-giardiniera 'Sweet Pete.'

A 1994 Seattle Times review of the original Queen Anne-area shop, founded about nine months earlier, praised the crusts and fresh-daily toppings -- whole-milk mozzarella, Ballard-made sausage, herbs chopped twice a day -- and highlighted inventive, novelty pies like a Thai-style peanut-sauce pizza alongside a build-your-own option.
